answer: Each candidate identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squarings, each dependent on the previous result, prevent GPUs from collapsing one chain into parallel work. An attacker can run clone chains concurrently, but each clone still requires its own sequential computation and hardware, imposing a physical time and resource cost rather than free identity multiplication. Even a terrace of clones must make the full voyage from challenge to proof; no shortcut lifts it from nadir to verification.
